recommendation.recommendation: Immediate field inspection combined with emergency irrigation and organic soil amendment to relieve severe water stress and restore vegetation vigor.
recommendation.justification: Satellite data shows critical vegetation stress (NDVI 0.154) and acute drought (NDWI -0.204) while weather, temperature, humidity and soil nitrogen are optimal. The lack of rainfall and low organic carbon are the primary constraints, increasing risk of disease and pest outbreaks. Prompt irrigation, mulching and organic amendment will allow the crop to exploit the favorable climate and market conditions (price up to 7618 INR/q).
actions: 1. Conduct a detailed field walk today: inspect all rows for symptoms of Fusarium wilt, Verticillium wilt, aphid colonies and bollworm damage; record incidence and severity.
2. Start emergency flood irrigation immediately (or drip if flood not feasible) to bring soil moisture to at least 70 % of field capacity; repeat every 7‑10 days during the current growth stage.
3. Apply a 5‑10 cm layer of well‑decomposed compost or farmyard manure across the plot to raise organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity.
4. Install straw or plastic mulch over the soil surface after irrigation to reduce evaporation and protect the canopy.
5. Follow the crop’s fertilizer schedule: apply a balanced N‑P‑K blend (e.g., 60‑30‑30 kg ha⁻¹) focusing on phosphorus and potassium, since nitrogen is already high.
6. Set up soil moisture sensors at 30 cm depth in three representative zones; record readings twice daily for the next two weeks.
7. Request a rapid‑refresh NDVI/NDWI satellite image (or use a handheld greenness sensor) 7 days after irrigation to verify canopy recovery.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture and improved water retention will raise NDVI above 0.4 within two weeks, reduce disease/pest pressure, and position the crop to achieve near‑optimal yields, enabling sale at the current favorable market price.

steps.finding: Immediate field inspection combined with emergency irrigation and organic soil amendment to relieve severe water stress and restore vegetation vigor.
actions: 1. Conduct a detailed field walk today: inspect all rows for symptoms of Fusarium wilt, Verticillium wilt, aphid colonies and bollworm damage; record incidence and severity.
2. Start emergency flood irrigation immediately (or drip if flood not feasible) to bring soil moisture to at least 70 % of field capacity; repeat every 7‑10 days during the current growth stage.
3. Apply a 5‑10 cm layer of well‑decomposed compost or farmyard manure across the plot to raise organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity.
4. Install straw or plastic mulch over the soil surface after irrigation to reduce evaporation and protect the canopy.
5. Follow the crop’s fertilizer schedule: apply a balanced N‑P‑K blend (e.g., 60‑30‑30 kg ha⁻¹) focusing on phosphorus and potassium, since nitrogen is already high.
6. Set up soil moisture sensors at 30 cm depth in three representative zones; record readings twice daily for the next two weeks.
7. Request a rapid‑refresh NDVI/NDWI satellite image (or use a handheld greenness sensor) 7 days after irrigation to verify canopy recovery.
steps.justification: Satellite data shows critical vegetation stress (NDVI 0.154) and acute drought (NDWI -0.204) while weather, temperature, humidity and soil nitrogen are optimal. The lack of rainfall and low organic carbon are the primary constraints, increasing risk of disease and pest outbreaks. Prompt irrigation, mulching and organic amendment will allow the crop to exploit the favorable climate and market conditions (price up to 7618 INR/q).
